latestIgtvVideos.title: Cleaning With Aqueous Ozone 🤔🦠
latestIgtvVideos.caption:
I recently purchased a spray bottle that promises to kill 99.9% of common household bacteria in 30 seconds 🙋‍♀️👌. So, of course, I had to put that to the test because as much as I want that to be true, it sounds a little *too good to be true* 🧐. Armed with some agar plates 🧫 and a healthy dose of curiosity, I tested some common surfaces #beforeandafter to see how well it performed. **BTW, This video is 💯% NON-SPONSORED.** 
.
.
I swabbed the surfaces before cleaning, and then used the spray bottle, which generates #aqueousozone on demand, waited 30 seconds, and wiped. I swabbed the clean surfaces, and transferred those samples to the agar plates. This video shows my results 3 days later. 🤗

Aqueous ozone works as a powerful sanitizer, deodorizer, and cleaner - all you need is tap water and electricity. **No cartridges or capsules**. After it’s done kicking some serious bacteria booty, it converts back into water and oxygen, making it a safe, non-toxic cleaning solution for any household. 
.
Aqueous ozone also isn’t NEW. Ozone water treatment has been used commercially since 1904, and is still used today. But, the proof is in the pudding, so I put this video together showing how well it worked in our house 👏. 
This cleaner has also been shown to demonstrate greater than 99.9% inactivation of Human Coronavirus 
229E/ATCC VR-740, a commercially available surrogate virus for the Human Coronavirus SARS-Cov-2 which causes the COVID-19 Disease within 30 seconds 🦠 🙌
Full review: SLAYathomemother.com/cleaning-with-ozonated-water
Spray bottle: @o3waterworks

I seriously used to avoid making pot roast because it just *sounded* fancy and complicated—and with three kids, “fancy and complicated” has never exactly fit our lifestyle. 😂

Eventually, I tried a few recipes to see what all the hype was about… and then decided to do what I do best: make it ridiculously simple, throw everything in, and hope for the best. 😂

Turns out, that’s now my favorite way to make it. 

And since we’ve had it on rotation this season I wanted to share it with you to help make YOUR sports season easier too 👏 so here it is, feel free to screenshot or make it your own. 

THROW-TOGETHER POT ROAST Recipe 🥰

Ingredients: 
- 1-2 onions (we use two, but we really like onions here and it’s a cheap ay to fill up more of the bowl 😉)
- 1 packet of onion soup mix
- baby carrots
- baby potatoes
- 32 oz. beef broth
- 2.00-2.75 lb. chuck roast (this is good for our family of 5 with little, a preteen, and a teenager, BUT if you have more family members or older kids, I’d recommend going up a size)

* Slice up your onions however you like. I quarter my onions and peel them to toss in. No cutting of the baby carrots or potatoes.
* Toss (rinsed) potatoes, carrots, and onions into crockpot.
* Sprinkle in onion soup mix (just 1 packet) all over.
* Pour in entire container of beef stock.
* Pre-sear your meat (optional). I highly recommend it because it just gives your dish that extra VA-VA-VOOM, you know? But in the spirit of ‘throw-together’ dishes...you can totally skip this step. Had to mention it, though.
* Lay chuck roast on top of veggies.
* Cook on LOW for about 10 hours (though I’ve pushed this to 12 hours before and still had great results). You just want that connective tissue to break down 😉

Serve with some rolls (store bought if you want a no effort option 💁‍♀️) to help fill up those bellies and soak up the leftover broth 😍.

The closer I get to YHWH, the more I realize that growth doesn’t always feel good.

Sometimes the pain comes from growing.

Sometimes it comes from growing apart.

And if I’m being transparent, some of what I’ve walked through over the last few years really shook my confidence.

It made me question myself in ways I hadn’t before. I replayed conversations. Wondered what I could have done differently. Questioned how people saw me and, at times, even let that affect how I saw myself.

And one of the hardest things I’m learning is that not everything needs my defense.

When you feel misunderstood, there’s such a strong urge to set the record straight. To explain your side. To confront. To demand answers. To make sure people know what really happened.

But Jesus already knows.

He saw the conversations I wasn’t in.
He saw the intentions behind the actions.
He saw what hurt.
He saw my own heart, too.
And He knows the whole story better than I ever could.

There is so much freedom in realizing I don’t have to chase down every misunderstanding or fight to control someone else’s version of me.

And slowly, I’m learning to rebuild my confidence somewhere much steadier - not in being liked, understood, included, or validated by everyone, but in knowing who I am in Christ.

I can keep walking. Keep growing. Keep asking God to refine my heart and trust Him with the rest.

Through all the twists and turns, I’m incredibly grateful for the people God has placed beside me - the ones who have loved me well, prayed for me, encouraged me, and reminded me who I am when I struggled to remember it myself.

Especially my husband, who has been my rock through all of it. 🤍

I’m still learning. Still growing. Still being humbled.

But I’m learning that whether I’m walking through the pain or celebrating the good, I’d rather be close to Jesus than understood by everyone.

He saw it.

And that’s enough for me. 🩷🙏

#YHWH #christianmom #JesusisLord❤️

I’m not sure what I thought this season of life would look like… but I’m pretty sure it wasn’t this. 😂

Somewhere along the way, life became homeschooling, running businesses, career changes, church commitments, kids in completely different stages, and approximately 738 trips back and forth to practices, classes, games, and activities every week.

The laundry is currently chilling in the dryer like it pays rent while we’re on the sidelines cheering for our kids. There’s probably something in my fridge that needed to be thrown away three days ago. And at least once a week, one of us asks, “Wait…what do we have tomorrow?” 😂

But I really love this life.

It doesn’t look much like the one we probably would’ve planned for ourselves years ago, but there’s something really beautiful about realizing that not every detour was actually a detour.

God has changed our plans, stretched us, surprised us, and brought us into a season we never could have mapped out ourselves.

It’s busy. It’s a little chaotic. The laundry may never actually get folded.

But these are the days. 🩷🫶

And I’m really, really grateful we get to do them together.

A new season is coming our way, mamas - and we’re mentally prepping for that shift.

New school schedules, sports, dinner menus, laundry demands, work obligations, less daylight 😆.

Even the most prepared person can get overwhelmed by so many changes, especially after the beautiful bliss of summertime, sunshine, and flexibility 🥰🫶🥹

I have to remind myself at the start of every season that I don’t have to have it all together, not everything has to get checked off my list, and I’m doing JUST FINE 😅🤘.

But if you’re needing some of these Home Reset Rules, too, they really help bring things back to perspective and keep you from burning out. Here they are again! 

My Home Reset Rules:

One room at a time.
Timer first.
Done beats perfect.
Every item needs a home.
Stop before burnout.

Save this post and share some of your reset rules with me below! 👇🩷✨

#tidyspacetidymind #cleaning #cleanhome #cleanwithmemotivation #roomreset

Pulled pork mini sandwiches for the win! Comment RECIPE 👇👇👇 and I’ll send you this one to copy/paste or screenshot 🥰

This is one of my favorite low effort family dinner meal ideas because the crockpot basically does all the work for me. No special prep, thawing, for forethought going into this one. We make this any season, and pair it with whatever we’re feeling like that day! 

Here’s what you need:
- half loin roast pork
- 2 lemons 🍋 
- seasoning of your choice 
- BBQ sauce 
- Hawaiian rolls 
- crockpot 

Don’t forgot to repurpose your lemon slices in a measuring cup or bowl of 2 cups of water and heat on HIGH for 5 minutes to help deep clean your microwave 😉 be careful as the water will be SUPER HOT. 🥵

I made my own custom car emblem using acrylic, my laser, and some 3M tape. 

This is my third time making one for our cars, and they stay put through car washes, rain, wind, hail 😆, wildfire smoke, all the Midwest adventures we go on, you name it. My husband’s has been on his car for two years now, my previous car had one on for 2.5 years, now it was time for decorate my new car :). 

 They hold up great and are so fun to make! 

Laser: @thunderlaserusa Nova Plus [thunderlaserpartner]
Material: 2 layers of 1/8” acrylic + double-sided 3M tape 

Be sure to clean your flat surface really well and apply pressure for a couple minutes. I would also avoid washing directly/rain for about 48 hours 😉 if that wasn’t obvious! 🫶
